newsitem.title: CANADA: NOVA unit plans C$25 mln Alberta gas plant.
newsitem.headline: NOVA unit plans C$25 mln Alberta gas plant.

text.p: NOVA Corp unit Novagas Clearinghouse Ltd said on Tuesday it planned to build a C$25 million natural gas processing plant at Zama Lake in northwestern Alberta.

The new plant, which was to be capable of processing 65 million cubic feet of gas a day, was slated to be on stream in the third quarter of 1997, pending reviews by the Alberta Energy and Utilities Board, NCL said.
NCL also said it reached an agreement to provide gathering and processing services for all gas produced by Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Pennzoil Canada Inc in the Zama region.

Under the deal, the midstream gas services firm will also assume management, operation and control of a 30 million cubic foot a day gas plant at Zama currently operated by Gulf, as well as 95 km of gas gathering pipelines.
The new processing facility will be the third facility at Zama for NCL.
In April 1995, the company completed a C$25 million, 65 million cubic foot per day processing facility adjacent to the Gulf/Pennzoil plant.
With the addition of the new NCL plant, the site will have a combined processing capacity of 160 million cubic feet per day, the company said. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
